Mark / team — thanks for the context. Below is a concise, redline‑friendly proposal keeping everything on Hosted API (no infra change required). We're trying to balance predictable unit economics while recognizing your potential growth. Numbers below are per‑token (USD) and apply to generation + embeddings as a blended price.

Proposed slab (monthly tokens):
- Tier A (0 — 200M): $0.0032 / token
- Tier B (200M — 1.25B): $0.0021 / token
- Tier C (1.25B — 5B): $0.0016 / token
- Tier D (>5B): custom enterprise band (negotiable, typically >= 20% off Tier C)

Pilot concession:
- 3‑month pilot at 120M tokens/mo baseline
- Pilot rate: 30% off Tier A (effective $0.00224/token) for pilot months only
- Pilot tokens not consumed may carry forward as credits for up to 60 days after pilot end (not to exceed total pilot token budget)

Commit & rollover mechanics (proposed):
- 12‑month term preferred; customer can select a Monthly‑Commit or Annual‑Commit billing pattern
- Monthly Commit: charged against slab monthly; unused tokens convert to credits valid for 60 days (no cash refunds)
- Annual Commit: invoice upfront with a 10% prepayment discount; unused tokens may be pooled across months in the contract year
- Overage: if monthly usage exceeds the top of your selected slab, excess billed at next tier rate; automatic burst protection available for spikes with credit drawdown

Operational guardrails and SLOs:
- Standard Hosted API SLOs apply; we can add latency targets if you require specific SLAs tied to committed volumes
- We'll provide token‑level cost dashboards and a monthly usage forecast review for your engineering team

Concessions and approvals:
- Naomi: finance has pre‑approved a pilot discount up to 30% and limited carry‑forward credits (60d) for pilots up to 150M/mo.
- Laura: CS will dedicate an onboarding window and a single performance review at the end of pilot.

Next steps:
1) If this looks reasonable, we'll send a redlineable rate table (CSV) and an updated SOW with the pilot concession language.
2) Procurement to confirm whether they want Monthly Commit or Annual Commit (affects billing/credit behavior).
3) Legal: quick contract addendum for pilot credits and rollover terms.

Open to tweaks — if you prefer a blended discount across the first 12 months instead of tiered slabs, we can sketch that quickly, but slabs give clearer marginal economics as you scale.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Pricing & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
